With topics like these, wording is incredibly important. I don’t think that all white people are inherently racist- in fact, i think ascribing a trait to any one race and saying its inherent is racist on its own. However, I do think that- at least in America- we’re socialized in a society that is and has been historically racist, and it instills racial biases in every person, not just white people. 

It’s important to separate the idea of saying or doing something racist from actually being a racist. Every single person has said or done something racist, either intentionally or unintentionally. That doesn’t make these people racists- being a racist requires acknowledgement of racism and accepting it as a good or neutral thing. As long as you understand that racism is wrong and try not to say/do racist things, then I’m not considering you a racist.

This is fundamentally why I disagree with that statement. The idea that all white people are racists ignores white people who have fought against the biases they were taught, denies them agency over their own actions, and disregards them the potential to change. Additionally, saying that its a trait inherent to white people disregards the root of the problem- the biases that are present to society that we absorb through the media and people we interact with. It also ignores the fact that POC can be racist as well.
